claims.quote: We have high towers; the highest about half a mile in height; and some of them likewise set upon high mountains; so that the vantage of the hill with the tower is in the highest of them three miles at least.
claims.description: Towers half a mile tall are built, some on mountains, reaching three miles above the lowlands.

claims.quote: We use these towers, according to their several heights, and situations, for insolation, refrigeration, conservation; and for the view of divers meteors; as winds, rain, snow, hail; and some of the fiery meteors also.
claims.description: High towers serve as observatories for studying weather and for cooling and preserving things at altitude.

claims.quote: We have also pools, of which some do strain fresh water out of salt; and others by art do turn fresh water into salt.
claims.description: Pools are used to desalinate seawater into fresh water, and to make fresh water salt.

claims.quote: and likewise engines for multiplying and enforcing of winds, to set also on going diverse motions.
claims.description: Machines that generate and strengthen wind are used to drive other machinery.

claims.quote: We have also a number of artificial wells and fountains, made in imitation of the natural sources and baths
claims.description: Artificial mineral springs reproduce natural medicinal waters by infusing minerals.

claims.quote: And amongst them we have a water which we call Water of Paradise, being, by that we do to it made very sovereign for health, and prolongation of life.
claims.description: A treated water greatly improves health and prolongs life.

claims.quote: We have also great and spacious houses where we imitate and demonstrate meteors; as snow, hail, rain, some artificial rains of bodies and not of water, thunders, lightnings; also generations of bodies in air; as frogs, flies, and divers others.
claims.description: Large buildings reproduce weather artificially: snow, hail, rain, thunder and lightning.

claims.quote: We have also certain chambers, which we call Chambers of Health, where we qualify the air as we think good and proper for the cure of divers diseases, and preservation of health.
claims.description: Rooms with specially conditioned air are used to treat diseases and preserve health.

claims.quote: We have also fair and large baths, of several mixtures, for the cure of diseases, and the restoring of man's body from arefaction
claims.description: Medicinal baths cure diseases, restore the withered body and strengthen sinews and organs.

claims.quote: And we make (by art) in the same orchards and gardens, trees and flowers to come earlier or later than their seasons; and to come up and bear more speedily than by their natural course they do.
claims.description: Plants are made to flower and fruit out of season and to grow and bear faster than nature allows.

claims.quote: We make them also by art greater much than their nature; and their fruit greater and sweeter and of differing taste, smell, colour, and figure, from their nature.
claims.description: Plants are made larger, with bigger, sweeter fruit of new taste, smell, color and shape.

claims.quote: We have also means to make divers plants rise by mixtures of earths without seeds
claims.description: Plants are made to grow from mixtures of soils without any seeds.

claims.quote: and likewise to make divers new plants, differing from the vulgar; and to make one tree or plant turn into another.
claims.description: New plant species are created, and one kind of plant is transformed into another.

claims.quote: We have also parks and enclosures of all sorts of beasts and birds which we use not only for view or rareness, but likewise for dissections and trials; that thereby we may take light what may be wrought upon the body of man.
claims.description: Animals are kept for dissection and experiments to learn what can be done to the human body.

claims.quote: as continuing life in them, though divers parts, which you account vital, be perished and taken forth
claims.description: Animals are kept alive after organs thought vital have been removed.

claims.quote: resuscitating of some that seem dead in appearance
claims.description: Animals that appear dead are revived (resuscitation).

claims.quote: We try also all poisons and other medicines upon them, as well of chirurgery, as physic.
claims.description: Poisons, medicines and surgical methods are tested on animals before use on people.

claims.quote: By art likewise, we make them greater or taller than their kind is; and contrariwise dwarf them, and stay their growth
claims.description: Animals are made larger than their kind, or dwarfed with their growth stopped.

claims.quote: we make them more fruitful and bearing than their kind is; and contrariwise barren and not generative.
claims.description: Animal fertility is controlled, making them more fertile or sterile at will.

claims.quote: We find means to make commixtures and copulations of different kinds; which have produced many new kinds, and them not barren, as the general opinion is.
claims.description: Crossbreeding different species produces fertile new hybrid species.

claims.quote: We make a number of kinds of serpents, worms, flies, fishes, of putrefaction; whereof some are advanced (in effect) to be perfect creatures, like bests or birds; and have sexes, and do propagate.
claims.description: New animals are created from decaying matter, with predictable results, and some become complete breeding creatures.

claims.quote: insomuch as some of them put upon the back of your hand will, with a little stay, pass through to the palm, and yet taste mild to the mouth.
claims.description: Drinks are made so fine that they pass right through the skin of the hand.

claims.quote: whereof some of the drinks are such, as they are in effect meat and drink both: so that divers, especially in age, do desire to live with them, with little or no meat or bread.
claims.description: Nourishing drinks act as complete meals, so people can live on them alone.

claims.quote: So for meats, we have some of them so beaten and made tender and mortified, yet without all corrupting, as a weak heat of the stomach will turn them into good chylus
claims.description: Meats are pre-processed so that even a weak stomach can digest them easily.

claims.quote: We have some meats also and breads and drinks, which taken by men enable them to fast long after
claims.description: Special foods let people go without eating for a long time afterward.

claims.quote: and some other, that used make the very flesh of men's bodies sensibly more hard and tough and their strength far greater than otherwise it would be.
claims.description: Foods toughen the body and make people far stronger than normal.

claims.quote: But above all, we have heats, in imitation of the Sun's and heavenly bodies' heats, that pass divers inequalities, and (as it were) orbs, progresses, and returns, whereby we produce admirable effects.
claims.description: Artificial heat sources imitate the sun's heat and its cycles.

claims.quote: Instruments also which generate heat only by motion.
claims.description: Devices produce heat purely from motion.

claims.quote: and out of things uncoloured and transparent, we can represent unto you all several colours; not in rain-bows, (as it is in gems, and prisms,) but of themselves single.
claims.description: Single pure colors of light are produced from colorless materials.

claims.quote: We represent also all multiplications of light, which we carry to great distance, and make so sharp as to discern small points and lines.
claims.description: Light is amplified and sent over great distances in a beam sharp enough to show fine points and lines.

claims.quote: We find also divers means, yet unknown to you, of producing of light originally from divers bodies.
claims.description: New ways of producing light from various substances are discovered.

claims.quote: We have also helps for the sight, far above spectacles and glasses in use.
claims.description: Vision aids far better than ordinary spectacles.

claims.quote: We have also glasses and means to see small and minute bodies perfectly and distinctly; as the shapes and colours of small flies and worms, grains and flaws in gems, which cannot otherwise be seen, observations in urine and blood not otherwise to be seen.
claims.description: Microscopes show tiny bodies clearly and reveal things in urine and blood for medical study.

claims.quote: and amongst them some of metals vitrificated, and other materials besides those of which you make glass.
claims.description: Glass is made from metals and other unusual materials.

claims.quote: Likewise loadstones of prodigious virtue
claims.description: Magnets of enormous strength.

claims.quote: We represent small sounds as great and deep; likewise great sounds extenuate and sharp; we make divers tremblings and warblings of sounds, which in their original are entire.
claims.description: Sounds are amplified, reduced, and altered with tremolo and warbling effects.

claims.quote: We represent and imitate all articulate sounds and letters, and the voices and notes of beasts and birds.
claims.description: Machines reproduce human speech sounds and animal and bird voices.

claims.quote: We have certain helps which set to the ear do further the hearing greatly.
claims.description: Devices placed at the ear greatly improve hearing (hearing aids).

claims.quote: We have also means to convey sounds in trunks and pipes, in strange lines and distances.
claims.description: Sound is carried through tubes and pipes over long and winding distances.

claims.quote: We imitate smells, making all smells to breathe outs of other mixtures than those that give them.
claims.description: Any smell is reproduced artificially from different ingredients (synthetic fragrances).

claims.quote: We make divers imitations of taste likewise, so that they will deceive any man's taste.
claims.description: Artificial flavors imitate tastes so well they fool anyone.

claims.quote: There we imitate and practise to make swifter motions than any you have, either out of your muskets or any engine that you have
claims.description: Machines and projectiles move faster than anything fired from a musket.

claims.quote: and to make them stronger and more violent than yours are; exceeding your greatest cannons and basilisks.
claims.description: Weapons more powerful than the largest cannons.

claims.quote: and likewise new mixtures and compositions of gun-powder, wild-fires burning in water, and unquenchable.
claims.description: New gunpowders and incendiaries that burn underwater and cannot be put out.

claims.quote: We imitate also flights of birds; we have some degrees of flying in the air.
claims.description: Flying machines that imitate birds achieve some flight.

claims.quote: We have ships and boats for going under water, and brooking of seas; also swimming-girdles and supporters.
claims.description: Submarines travel under water, and swimming belts keep people afloat.

claims.quote: We have divers curious clocks, and other like motions of return: and some perpetual motions.
claims.description: Perpetual motion machines exist.

claims.quote: But we do hate all impostures, and lies; insomuch as we have severely forbidden it to all our fellows, under pain of ignominy and fines, that they do not show any natural work or thing, adorned or swelling; but only pure as it is, and without all affectation of strangeness.
claims.description: Researchers are bound by rules, enforced by fines and disgrace, to present results honestly without exaggeration.

claims.quote: we have twelve that sail into foreign countries, under the names of other nations, (for our own we conceal); who bring us the books, and abstracts, and patterns of experiments of all other parts.
claims.description: Agents travel abroad in disguise to gather foreign books and experimental knowledge (scientific intelligence gathering).

claims.quote: We have three that draw the experiments of the former four into titles and tables, to give the better light for the drawing of observations and axioms out of them.
claims.description: Specialists organize collected experimental results into tables so general laws can be drawn from them.

claims.quote: We have three that bend themselves, looking into the experiments of their fellows, and cast about how to draw out of them things of use and practise for man's life, and knowledge
claims.description: A dedicated group turns research findings into practical applications (applied research).

claims.quote: we have three that take care, out of them, to direct new experiments, of a higher light, more penetrating into nature than the former.
claims.description: A research body reviews past results and directs new, deeper experiments, carried out by others who report back.

claims.quote: and take all an oath of secrecy, for the concealing of those which we think fit to keep secret: though some of those we do reveal sometimes to the state and some not.
claims.description: Researchers decide which discoveries to publish, swear secrecy over the rest, and withhold some even from the state.

claims.quote: For upon every invention of value, we erect a statue to the inventor, and give him a liberal and honourable reward.
claims.description: Every valuable invention earns its inventor a statue and a generous reward.

claims.quote: And we do also declare natural divinations of diseases, plagues, swarms-of hurtful creatures, scarcity, tempests, earthquakes, great inundations, comets, temperature of the year, and divers other things; and we give counsel thereupon, what the people shall do for the prevention and remedy of them.
claims.description: Scientists forecast epidemics, pests, famine, storms, earthquakes, floods and seasonal weather, and advise the public on prevention.
